name: Per-action autonomy
note: Act, ask, or hand off, per kind of action
summary: Instead of one autonomy level for the whole agent, each kind of action gets its own: act silently, act and report, ask first, or hand off to a person. The level is usually set by how reversible and costly the action is.
how: List the action types the agent can take (read, draft, send, pay, delete…)
Assign each a level: act, act and notify, ask, or hand off
Base the level on reversibility and blast radius
Promote an action type only after its approval history supports it
facts: Codex granular approval policy; AP2 human-present vs human-not-present payments; Stripe MCP requires human confirmation for refunds and outbound payments
Fewer pointless prompts, but needs an up-front catalogue of actions
goodFor: Assistants that both read and act (email, payments, ops)
Gradually widening autonomy as trust grows
watchOut: New tools default to the wrong level unless someone classifies them
Misclassifying an irreversible action as low-risk
